description: Build your own network of agents from Claude Code, Codex and Pi: persistent teams with roles, shared context and owned work.
rules: Install with npm install -g @loom/cli. Loom requires Node.js 22 or 24, tmux, and Claude Code or Codex signed in. The starter team uses both, and the kernel operator adapts it when you have only one.
Preview before launching: loom specs preview <spec>, then loom up <spec> --cwd . --plan, then loom up <spec> --cwd .
Check seat readiness with loom ps --nodes --rig <rig>, not only daemon health from loom status.
Inside a rig, an agent runs loom whoami --json first and treats its output as its identity.
loom send <session> "message" types into a peer's terminal and presses Enter; loom capture <session> reads that peer's screen.
Work another agent must act on goes in the queue (loom queue create or loom queue handoff); a message informs but does not assign work.
Use loom start to bring rigs back after a reboot or daemon restart.
Run loom --help for the current command surface; the CLI is authoritative over older examples.
